title: Power Lens Laboratory
summary: Work through the same five pieces of evidence three times, asking who decides, what counts as knowing, and who is believed. Each lens implies a remedy, and leaves something running.
learningObjectives: Apply three analyses of power to one body of evidence and identify what each brings into focus.
Name, for each framework, a specific feature of the case it leaves in shadow.
State the remedy each analysis implies and what that remedy would leave untouched.
Explain why a framework's blind spot follows from the commitment that makes it useful.
Transfer the analysis to a second case without naming any framework.
interactionTypes: evidence selection against a three-level key
privacy: Every selection is held in the browser tab only and discarded when the page is left; nothing is saved, stored or transmitted, and no score or judgement about the person using it is produced.
accessibilityNotes: Nothing is timed. The five-item case file is printed in full, once, as an ordered list above the laboratory, and the evidence picker repeats a one-line version of each item so the controls are usable without scrolling back. All controls are native checkboxes and radios in labelled fieldsets, and applying a lens with nothing selected produces an explanatory message rather than a bare error. The pinned primary is deliberately small - it carries the lens's central question while the learner works down the evidence. Item-by-item feedback names its band in words in every heading, with the coloured left rule as a redundant second cue. The comparison table is a real table with row headers in a scrollable wrapper. Stage progress is carried by the stage track with aria-current and a done state expressed in text. All changes are announced through the shell's polite live region. Headings run h1 to h5 without skipping, focus moves to the laboratory heading when it opens, targets are at least 2.75rem, forced-colours rules are provided, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths. Each lens now carries one judgement - which evidence it brings into focus. What it leaves less visible is stated in the feedback rather than asked as a second task, so all three lenses are reached before the comparison. Anything held back sits inside a native <details> element, reachable by keyboard in one step and announced as collapsed rather than being disabled.
readmeTopic: One institutional case, three analyses of power: what each makes visible, what each hides, and what each would have you change
simulationNotes: Brackwell College and Ferrand Borough Council are inventions written for this page; no real institution, incident, inquiry, document or person is described, and no number or quotation is drawn from any real case. Nothing is random and no model is run. Each of the five evidence items is marked core, partly or no for each of the three lenses, and the overlaps are deliberate: item 3 (the technicians who stopped reporting) is core to the first lens and defensible under both of the others, so a learner who selects it three times is agreed with three times. Core sets are items 1 and 3 for the first lens; item 2 for the second; items 4 and 5 for the third. The file carried nine items until version 1.2.0; four of them duplicated a row of the key already present (the survey protocol and the wellbeing summary both repeated the manual's definition, the risk register repeated the agenda item, and the distribution of reporters repeated the incident log), so the second of each pair taught nothing the first had not. What remains is one item per distinct move, plus the item that overlaps all three lenses, which leaves the second lens with a single core item and two overlaps. The key is one defensible reading of an invented case, written to make the contrasts sharp, and the page says so in the limitations. Theorist names appear only in the teaching notes, never in the task, so that a learner who has never met them can still do the analysis and a learner who has cannot shortcut it.
